title: MSA/DPA billability & SLA escalation review
summary: Quick vendor gating call to resolve MSA/DPA billing language, confirm SLA credits and escalation path, and align on pilot billing model. Agreed actions: send a redlined MSA snapshot, share pricing spreadsheet for committed vs on-demand, schedule security appendix deep-dive with Sophie next week.
topics: SLA uptime threshold and credit calculation
Billing model for pilot (non-prod vs prod)
KMS / keying options and privileged access
Onboarding timeline and pilot success metrics
questions: What counts as billable token for cached responses?
Can we get an SSO + SCIM onboarding window less than 30 days?
What is Redwood's rollback and fallback policy if Dedicated pool is saturated?
transcript: [00:00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the remaining MSA/DPA points and the SLA billing qu— billing models for the pilot with Marlow.

[00:00:12] Vikram Patel: Thanks Lena. We have Hannah and Sophie from legal and sec. I just want to be upfront— procurement's main blockers are liability cap language and the billability for dev vs prod traffic.
[00:00:29] Hannah Drew: Yeah, specifically the 30 day invoicing and the indemnity clause. We usually require a mutual indemnification for third party claims— is that something you can do?
[00:00:45] Lena Park: Right, so the standard Redwood MSA is one-way historically, but we can discuss. Diego, you want to add for the SLA side?

[00:00:54] Diego Ramos: Sure, hi. From the SLA perspective, customers ask about how credits are calculated— is it per-route, per-model, or global? Our default is per-route availability for hosted. For Dedicated we guarantee a 99.9 latency SLO and an uptime target— credits are pro-rated. Sometimes that wording trips buy-side legal because they expect service credits to be a direct dollar offset.
[00:01:23] Marcus Bell: Can you clarify the term 'per-route'? If we route some high-priority traffic to the Dedicated pool and fallback to Hosted, how are credits assessed?

[00:01:33] Diego Ramos: Good question. If the policy routes to Dedicated and fails over to Hosted, the fallback is considered a degradation event. Credits apply to the route's SLA— but the exception is if the fallback is a customer-configured policy. (laughter) Sorry, that's a mouthful. Essentially it's route-level unless specific routing policy says otherwise.

[00:01:55] Sophie Liu: Also from security, I need to confirm DPA retention windows. Our compliance requires 90 day retention for logs and 30 day deletion for user data. How does Redwood handle transient KV cache data and prompt logs?

[00:02:10] Lena Park: The platform supports configurable retention. For Hosted we default to 30 days for prompts/meta, but we can support 90-day retention as an add-on in the Private/ Dedicated agreements. Diego — KMS note?

[00:02:23] Diego Ramos: Right. If you bring your own key (BYOK) via KMS, we can ensure that stored artifacts are encrypted with customer-managed keys and we can support a longer retention SLA. Quick note — sometimes our transcripts mis-label KV cache as 'KV cash' in the docs, so just flag that— (brief chuckle).
[00:02:38] Hannah Drew: On billability— what's counted as billable tokens when caching/prefix reuse occurs? We don't want to be charged for obvious cache hits that are internal to test harnesses.

[00:02:50] Diego Ramos: We bill on generated and processed tokens at the route level. For prefix caching, we have a 'cache key' model— if a response is served from Redwood's prefix cache without extra compute, we often don't bill full compute but there is a small retrieval unit. I need to check the exact line in the price sheet; it's typically a fraction of a token unit. I'll attach a snippet.

[00:03:12] Vikram Patel: And for the pilot, procurement wants the pilot to be non-billable except for a capped 'compute credit' to test integration. Can Redwood accommodate a capped pilot that only bills above X?

[00:03:23] Lena Park: Yes, we can do usage credits and trial credits. The negotiation point is whether the pilot includes Dedicated capacity reservation or not. If you want dedicated GPUs reserved for the pilot window, that typically requires a short-term committed rate. If you're okay with ephemeral hosted capacity, we can do credits and on-demand billing for the pilot.
[00:03:43] Marcus Bell: For our throughput tests we need predictable latency at 1k reqs/min. Dedicated is attractive. What's the minimum commit?
[00:03:52] Lena Park: Typically we look at a monthly commit for Dedicated. For small pilots we can do a 30-day reserved min with pro-rated billing. Diego, on capacity —

[00:04:02] Diego Ramos: We can propose a small Dedicated pool sized to your expected concurrency— importantly, we keep autoscale buffers and fallback policies. If Dedicated is saturated we'll automatically route to a compatible hosted variant; that's the graceful degradation we mentioned. The fallback path is documented in the SLA appendix— which we'll share.
[00:04:21] Sophie Liu: About fallback: is data still encrypted with our keys when routed to Hosted? That's non-negotiable for us.

[00:04:29] Diego Ramos: If you use BYOK and the key is customer-controlled in a supported HSM/KMS, we can extend encryption to hosted fallback in specific modes, but there are limits across cloud regions. We'll need to map region residency to encryption policy— I'll flag that as an action.
[00:04:44] Hannah Drew: Liability cap — our legal is pushing for a 2x typical clause tied to fees. Redwood's standard is a fixed cap at subscription fees for 12 months. Is there room for mutuality?

[00:04:57] Lena Park: We're open to negotiating higher caps for enterprise agreements. The typical levers are either raise contract cap or add a carve-out for gross negligence. We'll surface standard alternatives in the redline.
[00:05:10] Vikram Patel: Timing — procurement needs the contract signed within 6 weeks to hit our Q3 integration. Is that timeline realistic?

[00:05:19] Lena Park: Yes, provided we get initial redlines this week and a security appendix meeting next Tuesday with Sophie. We can compress review to 4 weeks if legal and security run in parallel. Diego: any technical pre-reqs?

[00:05:31] Diego Ramos: From an onboarding perspective: SSO + SCIM, VPC peering for Dedicated, and a short benchmark run. SSO usually takes 10–14 business days depending on IdP. VPC peering and private routes need cloud approvals — that can add time, but it's doable in your window.
[00:05:48] Marcus Bell: VPC peering — our infra team will need egress controls. Does Redwood support customer-managed egress routing and egress IP allowlists?

[00:05:57] Lena Park: Yes, we support egress IP allowlists and custom egress via VPC NATs for Private deployments. For Hosted we provide fixed egress ranges and can do static egress IPs for Dedicated in select regions.
[00:06:10] Sophie Liu: Another question — audit logs retention. We need 365 days of immutable audit trails for access and token usage. Can that be scoped into the DPA?

[00:06:20] Diego Ramos: We can include audit retention as part of an enterprise addendum. For Private, on-prem, or VPC we can meet 365 days; for Hosted it's an add-on. We'll propose storage and retention costs in the pricing sheet.
[00:06:35] Hannah Drew: Also please confirm breach notification SLA — 72 hours? Our policy is 72 hours for initial notification and 30 day full report.
[00:06:44] Lena Park: Redwood's standard is 72 hours for incident notification; we can match your 30-day full report requirement in the DPA as an appendix.

[00:06:53] Vikram Patel: On pricing, procurement will want committed vs on-demand comparisons. Please include an example with hypothetical 1M tokens/month and a breakdown with quantization and batching savings. We need line items for Dedicated reserved vs Hosted on-demand.

[00:07:08] Lena Park: We'll send a pricing workbook. Diego will attach an expected unit cost and a model of batching improvements — that's where Redwood Optimize recommendations can cut unit cost. Diego?

[00:07:18] Diego Ramos: Yep, I'll include two scenarios: 1) Dedicated 2x V100 equiv pool with 1M tokens and 10ms median latency; 2) Hosted on-demand with caching and smart batching. Note that the quantization profile can impact model accuracy; we'll include a quality delta estimate.
[00:07:33] Marcus Bell: Accuracy delta — important. We don't want production regressions because of 4-bit quantization.
[00:07:39] Diego Ramos: Of course. That's part of the Optimize guidance — you can run a small eval suite during the pilot to measure regression and decide on quantization.
[00:07:46] Sophie Liu: For the security meeting next week, can you share the SOC2 report and the network topology diagram ahead of time?
[00:07:52] Lena Park: Yes — we'll share SOC 2 type II and the network diagram. Also the whitepaper on our Private deployment options. I'll put links in the follow-up note.

[00:08:02] Hannah Drew: A couple legal nitpicks: the DPA needs a clear data subprocessors list and a clause for data subject requests. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood supports data export in parquet or JSONL for portability?

[00:08:15] Diego Ramos: We support exports in JSONL and can do parquet for large bulk exports. Data subject access can be fulfilled through our export APIs — we'll include the API endpoints in the security appendix.

[00:08:30] Vikram Patel: Ok, to recap — procurement wants redlines by Friday; security appendix meeting next Tue; pricing workbook within 48 hours; pilot terms clarified including whether Dedicated reserved or Hosted credits. Anything else?
[00:08:44] Marcus Bell: One more technical — if we run a long-running session with KV cache across many users, how is tenant isolation guaranteed? We've seen noisy neighbor issues elsewhere.

[00:08:55] Diego Ramos: Tenant isolation is enforced at the runtime via namespace separation, encrypted caches per-tenant, and per-tenant rate-limits. There are hardware-backed isolation patterns for Dedicated that give an extra guarantee. I'll add a short snippet on isolation architecture in the appendix.
[00:09:12] Sophie Liu: Quick tangential — any compliance or export controls around training data if we later choose to fine-tune?

[00:09:18] Lena Park: Fine-tuning paths are governed by the DPA and additional infra agreements. For regulated data we generally advise private deployments or on-prem for fine-tuning. We'll avoid training on customer PII unless explicitly agreed.
[00:09:30] Vikram Patel: Great. Hannah, Sophie — any blocking asks from legal or sec?

[00:09:36] Hannah Drew: I just need the MSA redline and the DPA with subprocessors list. If Redwood can take the 72 hr breach clause and provide mutual indemnity language as a counter, we're good to move forward.
[00:09:48] Sophie Liu: From security — I'd like to do a short architecture walk with your infra lead. Tue or Wed next week works.

[00:09:56] Lena Park: Awesome. We'll get those items out. Quick note — procurement sometimes asks about escrow for keys; Redwood supports key escrow for a restricted subset of cases but prefers customer-managed KMS. We'll include options.

[00:10:08] Vikram Patel: Perfect. Any open competitor notes? We briefly looked at InferoAI's enterprise offering — they had different VAT and egress fee models. If Redwood can beat their egress pricing, that's helpful.
[00:10:20] Lena Park: We'll include an egress fee comparison. Diego will produce the workbook and I'll circulate the redline and SOC2.
[00:10:30] Hannah Drew: One micro ask — can you send the MSA in Word format so our redlines are tracked? PDFs slow us down.
[00:10:36] Lena Park: Will do.
[00:10:40] Vikram Patel: Alright, thanks all. Let's capture next steps.
[00:10:44] [CROSSTALK]

[00:11:00] Lena Park: (recap) Action items — send redlined MSA in Word, pricing workbook with committed vs on-demand scenarios and egress, schedule security appendix for Tue, attach SOC2 and network diagram, and prepare a short technical appendix on isolation and fallback behavior. Diego will add billing clarifications on cache hits and pilot credit language.
[00:11:25] Diego Ramos: I'll follow up with a short note on the exact token billing on cached responses — I want to avoid ambiguous language that blocks procurement.
[00:11:31] Vikram Patel: Good. We'll look for those by Friday. Meeting adjourned.
[00:11:38] Lena Park: Thanks everyone. Bye.
